items.title: The Folders Programming Language
items.raw_content: Created 2015 | Updated 2026 | One of Forty-Four Esolangs , by the creator of Rivulet and Velato Where directories are code and drive space is infinite About Folders is a non-textual language, where code is expressed in containment and order alone. The names of the folders are ignored, apart from alphabetical ordering. In other words, they are pure ordered trees . Inspired by the Whitespace language, Folders is devoted to the idea of dematerialized code. It began with the question What is more empty than a file with no visible text? The empty folder is clutter, an appendage with no purpose. In git, it is ignored entirely (for this reason, it is suggested that Folders programs put .gitignore files in their deepest reaches). items.raw_content: AI agents are very effective at finding vulnerabilities in our software. This includes the kernel (the proof checker) of the Lean proof assistant. We are strengthening the official kernel, adding new kernels, and building new tools that simplify rechecking your Lean developments with external kernels. Lean v4.35.0 comes with the lake check command. This command exports your development and rechecks it with leanchecker , the official Lean kernel without all the baggage around it. items.title: Predicting CVSS and CWE from CVE Descriptions with Fine-Tuned Small Language Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Tara Dixit, Jessie Dong, Summer Li

Until April 2026, the National Vulnerability Database labeled nearly every published Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entry with a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) v3.1 vector, a severity tier, and a Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) weakness type. Now, NIST enriches only the high priority CVEs, leaving many newly published vulnerabilities unlabelled with the classifiers that security teams use for patch triage. In CVE enrichment, we predict the eight base components of CVSS v3.1 vector, base score, severity tier, and CWE from the vulnerability's textual description alone. To prevent leakage between near-duplicate descriptions, all systems are trained only on CVEs published in 2022 and 2023. Results are evaluated on all 36,325 usable 2024 CVEs in the pinned NVD snapshot. All scores are either directly predicted, or calculated from predicted vectors using the CVSS formula. A fine-tuned 3.8B-parameter model Phi-3.5-mini, trained with LoRA in 2.5 hours on a single Apple M5 Pro chip, achieves 69.9% accuracy on severity and 70.9% on CWE. It matches the official vector exactly for 48.8% of test CVEs, outperforming TF-IDF logistic regression by 2.8 to 4.7 points on all accuracy metrics based on zero-exclusion paired bootstrap intervals. When we evaluate the base model with a zero-shot prompt, it achieves 20.8% accuracy on severity in a sample of 2,000 CVEs. In this same sample, its stated scores match its own vector precisely for only 3.4% of CVEs. However, deriving scores from predicted vectors boosts the critical recall of TF-IDF logistic regression from 50.7% to 73.3% with no additional cost. And since the errors of the fine-tuned model and TF-IDF affect different CVEs, at least one system matches the correct severity tier for 75.8% of test CVEs.
items.title_zh: 用微调小语言模型从 CVE 描述预测 CVSS 与 CWE
items.summary: With NIST now enriching only high-priority CVEs, the authors fine-tune a 3.8B-parameter Phi-3.5-mini with LoRA in 2.5 hours on a single Apple M5 Pro to predict CVSS v3.1 components, severity and CWE from CVE descriptions. On 36,325 2024 CVEs, it reaches 69.9% severity accuracy and 70.9% CWE accuracy.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Koki Takeshita, Kenji Uebayashi, Hikaru Tomonari, Masaya Tsunokake, Koichiro Yawata et al.

Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. In this work, we are the first to propose a learning method for LLM-based circuit generation that optimizes, not the quality of a single circuit, but the quality and diversity of the entire circuit set obtained through multiple generations in the PPA objective space. The proposed method consists of (1) a generation-based training pipeline that reformulates coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set into a sequential circuit generation problem, and (2) a reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) that measures how much a generated circuit contributes to the Pareto front. Evaluation on the RTLLM v2 benchmark shows that the proposed method achieves +13.3 percentage points in relative Hypervolume over a baseline without PPA optimization and +14.4 percentage points over a single-objective reinforcement learning method, while also demonstrating superiority in circuit diversity.
items.title_zh: 基于多目标强化学习与大语言模型的帕累托最优 RTL 代码生成
items.summary: The authors propose a multi-objective reinforcement learning method that trains an LLM to generate a diverse set of Pareto-optimal RTL circuits, using a hypervolume-contribution reward. On RTLLM v2 it gains 13.3 percentage points of relative hypervolume over a baseline without PPA optimization and 14.4 points over single-objective RL.

items.title: The Judge Can Debias Itself: Awareness and Self-Debiasing for Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge
items.raw_content:
Authors: Youbing Yin, Jingyu Wu, Anoop Kumar, Scott Novotney, Daben Liu et al.

LLM-as-a-Judge systems are increasingly employed for automated evaluation, yet remain susceptible to systematic biases that undermine their reliability. We demonstrate that the judge can effectively debias itself without additional training. We propose two lightweight strategies: bias-aware prompting, which explicitly alerts the judge to potential target biases prior to evaluation, and self-debiasing, in which the judge critiques the initial judgment for bias influence. To broaden the evaluation scope, we introduce three novel benchmarks--authority bias (fabricated citations), confidence bias (assertive phrasing), and formatting bias (structured presentation)--and evaluate across seven bias types in total. Across three frontier models, self-debiasing improves performance in 20 out of 21 model-bias combinations with gains up to 15 percentage points, while bias-aware prompting also yields consistent improvements. The recent fine-tuned external critic, however, does not generalize as reliably to the newly-introduced bias types (degradation observed in 5 out of 9 cases). Our findings demonstrate that prompting a judge to reason about bias, either preemptively or retrospectively, is a robust and generalizable approach for enhancing evaluation integrity.
items.title_zh: 评委能自我去偏：面向可靠 LLM-as-a-Judge 的偏差感知与自我去偏
items.summary: The paper shows that an LLM judge can reduce its own biases without additional training through bias-aware prompting and self-debiasing, improving 20 of 21 model-bias combinations across three frontier models by up to 15 percentage points.

items.title: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.raw_content:
Authors: Junru Zhu, Xin Chen, Hang Lyu, Jiayue Meng, Muzi Li et al.

Multi-agent LLM systems exchange messages before acting through tools, but message delivery, signing authority, and tool-side enforcement are separate trust boundaries. We represent them as communication, authorization, and execution structures, and use the authority cut to characterize the smallest independently compromised signer coalition that can construct a policy-valid false-claim proof under stated assumptions. Controlled paired hidden-state studies reveal four distinctions. First, no fixed-message routing contrast across four models meets the prespecified large-effect criterion; when relays rewrite messages, executed false-state action rates vary by model and route configuration. Second, presented source-identity cues do not uniformly increase protected-action selection across three models. Third, on invalid-proof cases, Nemotron and Llama request protected actions in 52.1% and 54.2% of trials, respectively, yet a deterministic tool gate commits none: request-level and commitment-level safety readouts diverge. Finally, a separate single-model authorization check shows that a false claim with a policy-valid compromised-signer proof can pass the gate, since proof validity is not factual truth. These findings motivate evaluating delivered information, qualified authorization, model proposals, and committed actions separately.
items.title_zh: 谁发言、谁授权、谁行动？理解多智能体 LLM 的信任边界
items.summary: The paper separates communication, authorization and execution trust boundaries in multi-agent LLM systems, finding that request-level and commitment-level safety readouts diverge and that a policy-valid compromised-signer proof can pass an authorization gate even when the claim is false.

items.title: CRISP: Progressive Illumination Curriculum for Recurrent Low-Light Video Enhancement with Semantic Priors
items.raw_content:
Authors: Ruirui Lin, Xin Yan Lim, Yini Li, Zhiming Liu, Nantheera Anantrasirichai

Low-light video enhancement requires the recovery of brightness, color, and fine spatial structures while preserving temporal coherence in the presence of noise and motion. Existing methods often struggle to balance these objectives, particularly in severely degraded regions. This paper presents CRISP, a recurrent framework trained using a progressive illumination curriculum. Its two-frame recurrent architecture propagates information across successive frames to exploit temporal context beyond the immediate input pair. During training, supervision progressively transitions from intermediate targets interpolated between the low-light input and the reference to the full reference, gradually increasing the required brightness and color correction. This curriculum stabilizes recurrent training without introducing additional inference cost and yields the largest performance improvement among the components evaluated in the ablation study. To further support structural reconstruction, the framework optionally incorporates frozen DINOv3 semantic features through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN)-style modulation, without fine-tuning the foundation model. Experiments on DID and BVI-RLV demonstrate that CRISP achieves the highest PSNR on DID and the highest SSIM on BVI-RLV among the evaluated methods, while maintaining computational efficiency.
items.title_zh: CRISP：带语义先验的渐进光照课程低光视频增强
items.summary: CRISP is a recurrent low-light video enhancement framework trained with a progressive illumination curriculum, optionally using frozen DINOv3 semantic features; it achieves the highest PSNR on DID and the highest SSIM on BVI-RLV among evaluated methods.

items.title: Torch-DPhys: A Torch-Native, MOOSE-Compatible Framework for Differentiable Physics Simulation and Hybrid Machine Learning Integration
items.raw_content:
Authors: Akzhol Almukhametov, Yang Liu

We present Torch-DPhys, a Torch-native framework implemented in PyTorch for differentiable physics simulation and hybrid physics-machine learning. It implements selected thermal-hydraulic modeling concepts and discretizations from MOOSE's Thermal Hydraulics Module and the System Analysis Module (SAM), with a preliminary extension to continuum mechanics. Native tensor residuals support CPU and GPU execution, compilation of selected numerical kernels, and sparse direct linear solves. Sensitivities are obtained by differentiating executed numerical operations or through discrete adjoints of converged residual equations. Verification combines analytical solutions, reference-code comparisons, and derivative checks. Demonstrations cover plane-strain elasticity, one- and two-loop thermal-hydraulic transients, and an axisymmetric molten-salt fast reactor. For the reactor, comparison with SAM-Lite gives a maximum normalized field discrepancy of 1.13 x 10^-5 over 200 adaptive time steps, demonstrating agreement between the tested discrete implementations. Selected transient sensitivities are assessed using tangent-linear calculations and finite differences on fixed time schedules. Two applications illustrate the framework's connection between simulation and optimization. A residual-adjoint parameter-identification calculation recovers nominal pump head and heating power with relative errors below 0.06% from noiseless synthetic MOOSE observations. A separate three-loop plant demonstration uses solver-in-the-loop training of a predictive controller by differentiating trajectory-level objectives through the thermal-hydraulic simulation. These examples illustrate a foundation for gradient-based inference, control, and coupled physics-machine learning models in nuclear engineering.
items.title_zh: Torch-DPhys：兼容 MOOSE 的 Torch 原生可微物理仿真框架
items.summary: Torch-DPhys is a PyTorch-native framework for differentiable physics simulation that implements thermal-hydraulic models from MOOSE and its System Analysis Module, with CPU and GPU execution and gradient-based parameter identification and control.

items.title: CME-SpectrumBench: Can LLMs Analyze Condensed Matter Spectral Data?
items.raw_content:
Authors: Jin Gene Wong, Anjney Midha, Joseph Mathew Tennyson, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica et al.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are presently well assessed by expert-level mathematics and physics benchmarks which focus on theoretical, symbolic reasoning. However, we lack experimental benchmarks that evaluate data analysis in frontier research problems, a capability that future domain-specific foundation models must have. To this end, we present CME-SpectrumBench, an expert-designed benchmark consisting of 190 questions that measures how reliably frontier LLMs analyze research-level spectral scientific data in condensed matter experiments (CME). Using simulated CME spectral data, we prompt models to identify structures from 2D intensity arrays in the face of noise and limited instrumental resolution, a test of dense context reasoning. Models are scored by how accurately their numerical answers approach the ground truth. Under direct query, scores generally pale in comparison to handwritten code due to clear failure modes: models can find simple features but struggle to trace patterns or compute derived quantities, and performance typically degrades with increased data resolution and noise/convolution levels. LLM performance becomes comparable to handwritten code by allowing tool use (access to a Python interpreter) with/without ReAct prompting, in effect mapping questions onto agentic code generation problems. Our findings show that frontier models can serve as research assistants by interfacing with data through code, but still face difficulties processing information directly from large datasets - a key barrier future foundation models must overcome. The code and data are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/jingene/CMESpectrumBench.
items.title_zh: CME-SpectrumBench：LLM 能否分析凝聚态光谱数据？
items.summary: The authors introduce CME-SpectrumBench, 190 expert-designed questions that test whether frontier LLMs can analyze simulated condensed-matter spectral data. Models do much better when allowed to use a Python interpreter, approaching handwritten code.

items.title: Morpheus-2.0: Multiscale Probabilistic Forecasting with Dual-Axis Attention
items.raw_content:
Authors: Aakriti, Manoj Cherukumalli, Prathamesh Patil, Leonidas Tsepenekas, Amit Varshney et al.

A universal forecaster is trained once and applied everywhere, so it must serve tasks whose schemas, forecast horizons, and temporal resolutions all differ. The number of targets and covariates changes from dataset to dataset, horizons vary by orders of magnitude, and sampling rates range from seconds to years. Existing time-series foundation models address these only in part, since they isolate each series or visit the two grid relations in separate blocks, and they fix the horizon and resolution before training begins. We introduce Morpheus-2.0, a compact encoder-only foundation model that represents targets and covariates on a single variable-time grid. Its dual-axis attention runs both relations side by side in every layer, one across variables at a timestep and one across time within a variable; a learned gate weights the two per layer, and an axis-aware rotary encoding preserves both grid coordinates. The forecast length is sampled during training, so one set of weights spans short to long horizons at no additional inference cost. Morpheus-2.0 Multiscale extends the model to several temporal resolutions at once, weighting them according to the series being forecast. Across GIFT-Eval, which spans several domains and frequencies, the two models give complementary operating points: Morpheus-2.0 attains 0.685 relative MASE with 81M parameters, while the larger Morpheus-2.0 Multiscale attains 0.646 relative MASE and 0.455 relative CRPS, the lowest of any published system on both metrics.
items.title_zh: Morpheus-2.0：基于双轴注意力的多尺度概率预测
items.summary: Morpheus-2.0 is a compact encoder-only time-series foundation model with dual-axis attention that samples forecast length during training. On GIFT-Eval, the 81M-parameter model reaches 0.685 relative MASE, while Morpheus-2.0 Multiscale reaches 0.646 relative MASE and 0.455 relative CRPS.

items.title: Continuous Ontology Assurance through External Resources -- An Ontology Engineering Method with a Case Study in Software Language Engineering
items.raw_content:
Authors: Ralf Lämmel

Domain ontologies require review against knowledge recorded in evolving external resources. We propose COATER, a method that manages executable review components called arrows. Each arrow compares a scoped part of an ontology with a relevant resource and reports support or challenges to its axioms. Challenges may prompt proposals for completion, correction, or restructuring and become tasks for human or agent-assisted triage. Per-axiom coverage summarizes the assessments. We illustrate COATER with the FSL ontology in software language engineering (SLE): arrows review language coverage, language conceptualization, and software-engineering activities. An LLM-assisted linkage exercise increases compliance with a defined Wikipedia-linkage policy from 405 to 600 of 600 entities. A structured catalogue of SLE resources organizes review opportunities.
items.title_zh: 借助外部资源持续保障本体质量：软件语言工程中的本体工程方法
items.summary: The paper proposes COATER, a method that manages executable review components called arrows to check ontology axioms against evolving external resources. In an FSL ontology case study, an LLM-assisted linkage exercise raised Wikipedia-link compliance from 405 to 600 of 600 entities.

items.title: MAC units for a 2x2 int8 systolic array on Tiny Tapeout
items.raw_content:
Authors: Danila Gorodecky

We take the multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit of an open-source 2$\times$2 int8 systolic array taped out on Tiny Tapeout (GF180 process) and propose two replacements. The first one, \emph{hybrid}, uses a different arithmetic structure for each row of the array. It reduces the logic area of one MAC unit by 4--6\% and of the whole chip by 0.7--3.2\% after place and route. The second one, \emph{fused\_eq}, never builds the long carry chain of the accumulation. It shortens the critical path by 20\% for one MAC unit and by 14\% for the whole chip. All numbers come from the standard Tiny Tapeout flow (LibreLane) run in GitHub Actions. Correctness is checked by exhaustive simulation of all $2^{24}$ inputs, a formal equivalence proof, and the original test bench.
items.title_zh: Tiny Tapeout 上 2×2 int8 脉动阵列的 MAC 单元设计
items.summary: The paper proposes two replacements for the MAC unit of an open-source 2×2 int8 systolic array taped out on Tiny Tapeout (GF180): a hybrid design that cuts MAC logic area by 4–6%, and fused_eq, which shortens the critical path by 20% for one MAC unit, both verified by exhaustive simulation and a formal equivalence proof.
